speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you've had occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty. To help me understand what's going on, have you noticed any fluid drainage, fever, or worsening redness around your ear since the surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned shooting pain when eating; does this sensation radiate specifically to your ear, and do you experience any clicking or popping sounds in that ear? Additionally, have you noticed any discharge from the surgical site or a change in your hearing since your recent audiology test?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain you describe when eating sounds like it could be related to the jaw joint affecting your ear; do you also experience clicking, popping, or a feeling of the jaw locking when you move it? Furthermore, has the discomfort when wearing earrings improved, worsened, or stayed the same since your last visit?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (Gasserian ganglion irritation) secondary to post-tympanoplasty granulation tissue or scarring. The shooting pain triggered by chewing (eating) is the hallmark sign, and the earring discomfort suggests localized inflammation or nerve involvement at the mastoid/ear canal interface. I am ready to review images of the surgical site if you wish to confirm the presence of granulation tissue.
